 Cailleach Bhearra, (01 Caillech Btirri), "The Veiled Woman [or, Hag) of Beare
[a region in County Cork]," is what the speaker of a very long ninth-century
poem calls herself. She laments her transformation from youth and beauty
to decrepitude (as perhaps a nun or anchoress). The poem has been read
literally, as the reminiscences of an aged nun, and allegorically, as Christian
Ireland sighing for its pagan past. The figure of the old woman entered
the popular imagination and became fused with "hag" folktales. She surfaces
